evals.name: top-spenders-default-window
evals.prompt: What's costing the most in Databricks right now?
evals.expected_output: Since no window was given, defaults to the last 30 days, pulls Databricks-task run data via Orchestra MCP tools (list_pipeline_runs plus task/operation detail), and returns a ranked table of the top 10 jobs/pipelines by cost or cost-proxy with % of total spend and trend vs the prior period, followed by 2-3 sentences on anything trending up sharply.
assertions: Defaults to a 30-day lookback window since the user did not specify one
Uses Orchestra MCP tools (e.g. list_pipeline_runs) to gather real run data rather than estimating or guessing durations/costs
Returns a ranked table with columns for job/pipeline, avg cost or cost-proxy, % of total spend, and trend vs prior period
Limits the ranked table to the top 10
States explicitly whether figures are exact billing-system figures or a duration-based cost-proxy, rather than presenting a proxy as an exact dollar cost
Does not recommend specific fixes (e.g. rightsizing, cluster changes) -- points to the cluster-review/job-optimisation skills instead
Follows with a short (2-3 sentence) narrative on anything trending up sharply, not just the bare table

evals.name: weekly-trend-review
evals.prompt: Give me this week's Databricks cost review -- I want to know what's trending up compared to last week.
evals.expected_output: Scopes the review to the requested weekly window, computes each top job's trend against the prior window of the same length (up/down/flat with %), and clearly separates 'still a top spender' jobs from ones that are newly trending up.
assertions: Uses a window matching 'this week' (7 days) rather than silently defaulting to 30 days when the user specified weekly
Computes trend vs the prior window of the same length (not vs an arbitrary or unstated baseline)
Reports trend direction and percentage, not just up/down without magnitude
Distinguishes jobs that are consistently large spenders from jobs that are newly trending up this week
Uses Orchestra MCP tools to gather actual run data rather than estimating figures

evals.name: anomaly-vs-driver-distinction
evals.prompt: One of our jobs is always our biggest Databricks cost -- that's expected. But I have a feeling something else spiked recently. Can you check?
evals.expected_output: Ranks the top spenders as usual but explicitly separates 'expected top spender, not anomalous' from a distinct anomaly flag: any job whose cost/duration jumped materially more than its own historical volatility would suggest, calling that out separately from the top-N listing and pointing to the cluster-review/job-optimisation skills for a fix.
assertions: Does not flag the consistently-largest job as anomalous just because it is the top spender
Identifies anomalies based on a job's jump relative to its own historical volatility, not just absolute cost rank
Presents the anomaly flag separately from the top-10 ranked table rather than conflating the two
Points to the cluster-review or job-optimisation skills for remediation rather than attempting to fix the anomaly itself
Uses real run data via Orchestra MCP tools rather than guessing which job spiked

evals.name: no-exact-dbu-cost-available
evals.prompt: Which Databricks jobs are costing us the most? We don't have a Databricks SQL/system-tables integration connected, just Orchestra.
evals.expected_output: Falls back to a duration x cluster-size cost-proxy score per job since exact DBU $ cost isn't available from Orchestra metadata alone, clearly labels the ranking as a proxy rather than a billed dollar figure, and does not claim access to system.billing.usage that isn't actually connected.
assertions: Uses duration x cluster-size (or an equivalent metadata-based proxy) as the ranking basis since no billing system-tables integration is available
Clearly labels the figures as a cost-proxy, not an exact billed dollar amount
Does not claim to query system.billing.usage or system.billing.list_prices when the user said that integration isn't connected
Does not fabricate a specific dollar cost figure to fill the gap
Still produces a usable ranked top-10 list based on the available proxy metadata
